subject: Customer update: runtime disruption, immediate mitigation & follow-up plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: SEV-2 — runtime degradation observed (opening bridge)

Folks,

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and token error rates for the inference fleet serving Nimbus Retail beginning ~07:50 PST. Error rates spiked from ~0.2% to ~3.6% and median p95 latency jumped by ~2.1x on the 8-token trimmed requests. Impact is currently scoped to the us-west-2 region and predominantly the customer route for nimbus-prod.

I'm opening an ops bridge now (Zoom + Slack #ops-bridge) — joining: infra, runtime, and CS for customer comms. Initial observations:
- Metric: token error type "kv-cache-miss" correlating with a model shard reshuffle on autoscaler event.
- Affected: Nimbus Retail (heavy short-sequence inference), small fraction of other tenants saw transient spikes.
- Mitigation in progress: disable aggressive autoscale policies for the pool and pin model variant to q4-compat for affected nodes.

Immediate asks: 
- Diego: please bring up the pinned variant and hold scaling while we stabilize.
- Chloe: customer-facing exec note + single point update to Nimbus. Keep it calm, include ETA and safety steps.
- Marissa: alert Nimbus CS contact and confirm who we should include externally.

Attaching a short tail of bridge logs.

Attachment: bridge-log-tail.txt

Hannah
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: kate.leland@nimbusretail.com, ops@nimbusretail.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Update for Nimbus Retail — service impact and immediate steps

Kate / Nimbus Ops team,

I wanted to provide a concise update while our engineers work the bridge.

What happened (high level):
- Starting at ~07:50 PST today we detected elevated error rates and latency for inference requests routed to the us-west-2 pool used by your production service.
- Root cause under investigation but initial correlation points to a model shard reshuffle combined with an autoscaling event that caused elevated cache miss rates.

Impact:
- Some requests experienced higher latency and occasional generation failures (~3% of your traffic at peak). We do not have evidence of data loss or cross-tenant exposure.

What we are doing now:
- Holding autoscale actions and pinning the pool to a fallback model variant that avoids the reshuffle path.
- Rolling targeted restarts to restore normal KV cache behavior.
- Prioritizing your production traffic on remaining healthy nodes to reduce queueing.

Customer-facing commitments:
- Next status update: within 60 minutes (or sooner if we restore).
- If we do not see restoration within 90 minutes, we will schedule a 1:1 follow-up with your SREs and provide a temporary config you can apply to route traffic to an unaffected region.

We realize this is impacting your customers and sincerely apologize. We are treating this as a Sev-2 incident with priority escalation to engineering and CS.

I will send a follow-up with a timeline of mitigation steps and a link to the post-incident review doc.

Attachment: customer-incident-summary.pdf

—
Chloe Martin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com

From: Kate Leland <kate.leland@nimbusretail.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: ops@nimbusretail.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Update for Nimbus Retail — service impact and immediate steps

Thanks for the quick note, Chloe.

We appreciate the transparency. Two asks while you stabilize:  
1) Can you confirm whether any inference requests were retried on our behalf (we observed duplicate downstream orders during the spike)?
2) If there is any chance of user-facing data being retried or duplicated, we need to know to roll back or dedupe on our side.

We'd also like to schedule the 1:1 if the issue persists past your 90-minute window — please propose times.

Kate
Head of Platform, Nimbus Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: kate.leland@nimbusretail.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Update for Nimbus Retail — service impact and immediate steps (post-incident coordination)

Chloe / team — quick coordination note as we move toward resolution: 

Status: bridge reports steady improvement after pin + restart, error rate down to ~0.4% and p95 latency trending back to baseline. Diego, please confirm when you shift to remediation phase so I can prepare the post-incident comm and 1:1 scheduling.

Action items I propose for post-incident:
- Internal postmortem draft (owner: Diego) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Customer-facing executive summary and replay (owner: Chloe) — ready for review within 24 hours.
- Technical runbook update (owner: Runtime team) — include autoscale guardrails.
- 1:1 with Nimbus SREs to review impact and any dedup semantics (owner: Marissa) — propose Wed 2026-12-02 10:00-10:30 PST.

I'll open the postmortem doc and link it here: https://drive.google.com/incident-nimbus-20261130 (internal view). Please add notes and assign follow-ups inline.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kate.leland@nimbusretail.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident technical summary & next steps — Nimbus Retail incident (root cause and mitigations)

Kate / Team,

Following up with the technical summary and next steps from our postmortem draft. This consolidates what we discussed on the bridge and items we'll complete as part of remediation.

Root cause (short):
- A concurrent autoscaling action triggered a model shard reshuffle while certain nodes were mid-compaction. This produced a transient KV cache invalidation pattern that increased cache misses for short-sequence workloads and caused elevated error/latency for a slice of traffic.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Disabled autoscale for the affected pool and pinned to q4-compat variant.
- Performed staged restarts to rewarm KV caches and reduce incoherent state.
- Prioritized Nimbus routes while backlog drained.

Confirmed customer impact:
- Peak ~3% request failures between 07:50-08:35 PST on 2026-11-30. We did not find evidence of cross-tenant data exposure or persistent data loss. We are investigating potential duplicate downstream events and will provide a dedup report by the 1:1.

Remediation plan / timeline:
- Today: finalize postmortem draft and circulateto internal approvers (done).
- 2026-12-02: 1:1 with Nimbus SREs (Marissa to coordinate) to review dedup analysis and mitigations.
- 2026-12-08: runtime patch to autoscaler: add guardrail to block reshuffles during compactions and add a pre-check for KV cache stability.
- 2026-12-15: release owner sign-off and rollout to all regions.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (internal)

I'll attach the dedup analysis after we've completed the request-trace reconciliation — target EOD 2026-12-02. Thanks for your patience and we'll keep this tightly coordinated.

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
